sanskrit: ity uktā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasās te mahābalāḥ ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve rāvaṇaṃ rākṣaseśvaram
english: Having been thus addressed by the lord of rākṣasas, those mighty rākṣasas all spoke with folded hands to Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: rājan parighaśaktyṛṣṭiśūlapaṭṭasasaṃkulam sumahan no balaṃ kasmād viṣādaṃ bhajate bhavān
english: O king, our great army is filled with iron clubs, spears, javelins, tridents, and broadswords — why then does despondency overtake you?

sanskrit: kailāsaśikharāvāsī yakṣair bahubhir āvṛtaḥ sumahat kadanaṃ kṛtvā vaśyas te dhanadaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: Kubera, who dwelt on the peak of Kailāsa surrounded by many yakṣas, was reduced to your subjection after great slaughter was wrought.

sanskrit: sa maheśvarasakhyena ślāghamānas tvayā vibho nirjitaḥ samare roṣāl lokapālo mahābalaḥ
english: That guardian of the world, boasting of his friendship with Maheśvara, was defeated by you in fury in battle, O mighty one.

sanskrit: vinihatya ca yakṣaughān vikṣobhya ca vigṛhya ca tvayā kailāsaśikharād vimānam idam āhṛtam
english: Having slain the hosts of yakṣas, having routed and seized them, you brought away this aerial chariot from the peak of Kailāsa.

sanskrit: mayena dānavendreṇa tvadbhayāt sakhyam icchatā duhitā tava bhāryārthe dattā rākṣasapuṃgava
english: Maya, the lord of dānavas, desiring alliance out of fear of you, gave his daughter to be your wife, O bull among rākṣasas.

sanskrit: dānavendro madhur nāma vīryotsikto durāsadaḥ vigṛhya vaśam ānītaḥ kumbhīnasyāḥ sukhāvahaḥ
english: Madhu by name, the lord of dānavas, proud of his valour and hard to withstand, was seized and brought under your control — he who was the source of joy to Kumbhīnasī.

sanskrit: nirjitās te mahābāho nāgā gatvā rasātalam vāsukis takṣakaḥ śaṅkho jaṭī ca vaśam āhṛtāḥ
english: The nāgas who had retreated to the netherworld were defeated by you, O great-armed one; Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Śaṅkha, and Jaṭī were brought under your subjection.

sanskrit: akṣayā balavantaś ca śūrā labdhavarāḥ punaḥ tvayā saṃvatsaraṃ yuddhvā samare dānavā vibho
english: Those dānavas who are inexhaustible, powerful, heroic, and doubly blessed with boons — you fought them in battle for a full year, O mighty one.

sanskrit: svabalaṃ samupāśritya nītā vaśam ariṃdama māyāś cādhigatās tatra bahavo rākṣasādhipa
english: Relying on your own strength, they were brought to subjection, O slayer of foes; and many magical powers were also obtained there, O lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śūrāś ca balavantaś ca varuṇasya sutā raṇe nirjitās te mahābāho caturvidhabalānugāḥ
english: The heroic and mighty sons of Varuṇa, followed by their fourfold armies, were defeated by you in battle, O great-armed one.

sanskrit: mṛtyudaṇḍamahāgrāhaṃ śālmalidvīpamaṇḍitam avagāhya tvayā rājan yamasya balasāgaram
english: Having plunged into the ocean of Yama's army — terrible as the great crocodile of death's rod, adorned by the Śālmalī island — O king,

sanskrit: jayaś ca viplulaḥ prāpto mṛtyuś ca pratiṣedhitaḥ suyuddhena ca te sarve lokās tatra sutoṣitāḥ
english: great victory was obtained and death itself was repelled; by your glorious fighting all the worlds there were thoroughly gratified.

sanskrit: kṣatriyair bahubhir vīraiḥ śakratulyaparākramaiḥ āsīd vasumatī pūrṇā mahadbhir iva pādapaiḥ
english: The earth was filled with many heroic kṣatriyas of valour equal to Śakra, like great trees filling a forest.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vīryaguṇotsāhair na samo rāghavo raṇe prasahya te tvayā rājan hatāḥ paramadurjayāḥ
english: Those supremely hard-to-conquer ones, in whose might, virtue, and energy Rāghava has no equal in battle — they were forcibly slain by you, O king.

sanskrit: rājan nāpad ayukteyam āgatā prākṛtāj janāt hṛdi naiva tvayā kāryā tvaṃ vadhiṣyasi rāghavam
english: O king, this calamity that has come from an ordinary mortal is unworthy of concern; do not take it to heart — you shall slay Rāghava.

sanskrit: tato nīlāmbudanibhaḥ prahasto nāma rākṣasaḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ śūraḥ senāpatis tadā
english: Then Prahasta, a rākṣasa dark as a rain-cloud, that hero who was commander of the army, spoke with folded hands:

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvāḥ piśācapatagoragāḥ na tvāṃ dharṣayituṃ śaktāḥ kiṃ punar vānarā raṇe
english: Gods, dānavas, gandharvas, piśācas, birds, and serpents are incapable of assailing you — much less vānaras in battle.

sanskrit: sarve pramattā viśvastā vañcitāḥ sma hanūmatā na hi me jīvato gacchej jīvan sa vanagocaraḥ
english: All of us were careless and unsuspecting; we were deceived by Hanūmat. That forest-dweller shall not escape alive while I live.

sanskrit: sarvāṃ sāgaraparyantāṃ saśailavanakānanām karomy avānarāṃ bhūmim ājñāpayatu māṃ bhavān
english: I shall make all the earth up to the ocean, with its mountains, forests, and groves, free of vānaras — let your lordship command me.

sanskrit: rakṣāṃ caiva vidhāsyāmi vānarād rajanīcara nāgamiṣyati te duḥkhaṃ kiṃ cid ātmāparādhajam
english: I shall also provide protection from the vānaras, O ranger of the night; no grief arising from your own fault shall come upon you.

sanskrit: abravīc ca susaṃkruddho durmukho nāma rākṣasaḥ idaṃ na kṣamaṇīyaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ naḥ pradharṣaṇam
english: Then Durmukha, a rākṣasa in violent rage, declared: "This affront to all of us is truly intolerable —

sanskrit: ayaṃ paribhavo bhūyaḥ purasyāntaḥpurasya ca śrīmato rākṣasendrasya vānarendrapradharṣaṇam
english: this further insult to the prosperous lord of rākṣasas and to the city and its inner chambers — the brazen affront of the lord of vānaras.

sanskrit: asmin muhūrte hatvaiko nivartiṣyāmi vānarān praviṣṭān sāgaraṃ bhīmam ambaraṃ vā rasātalam
english: In this very moment I shall slay the vānaras — whether they have entered the terrible sea, the sky, or the netherworld — and return alone."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt susaṃkruddho vajradaṃṣṭro mahābalaḥ pragṛhya parighaṃ ghoraṃ māṃsaśoṇitarūpitam
english: Then Vajradaṃṣṭra, immensely strong and in violent rage, seizing a dreadful iron club reddened with flesh and blood, spoke:

sanskrit: kiṃ vo hanumatā kāryaṃ kṛpaṇena tapasvinā rāme tiṣṭhati durdharṣe sugrīve sahalakṣmaṇe
english: "What need have you of that wretched, hapless Hanūmat? While formidable Rāma stands firm with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa,

sanskrit: adya rāmaṃ sasugrīvaṃ parigheṇa salakṣmaṇam āgamiṣyāmi hatvaiko vikṣobhya harivāhinīm
english: today I shall come back alone, having routed the army of vānaras and slain Rāma with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa with my iron club."

sanskrit: kaumbhakarṇis tato vīro nikumbho nāma vīryavān abravīt paramakurddho rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam
english: Then Nikumbha, the heroic and mighty son of Kumbhakarṇa, in supreme fury, spoke to Rāvaṇa, the one who makes the world cry:

sanskrit: sarve bhavantas tiṣṭhantu mahārājena saṃgatāḥ aham eko haniṣyāmi rāghavaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam
english: "Let all of you remain assembled together with the great king; I alone shall slay Rāghava with Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tato vajrahanur nāma rākṣasaḥ parvatopamaḥ kruddhaḥ parilihan vaktraṃ jihvayā vākyam abravīt
english: Then Vajrahanu, a rākṣasa like a mountain, enraged and licking his mouth with his tongue, spoke:

sanskrit: svairaṃ kurvantu kāryāṇi bhavanto vigatajvarāḥ eko 'haṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi tān sarvān hariyūthapān
english: "Let your lordships attend freely to your affairs without anxiety; I alone shall devour all those chiefs of vānara troops."

sanskrit: svasthāḥ krīḍantu niścintāḥ pibantu madhuvāruṇīm aham eko haniṣyāmi sugrīvaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam sāṅgadaṃ ca hanūmantaṃ rāmaṃ ca raṇakuñjaram
english: "Be at ease, take sport without care, drink honey-wine; I alone shall slay Sugrīva with Lakṣmaṇa, and Aṅgada, Hanūmat, and Rāma, the elephant of the battlefield."

sanskrit: tato nikumbho rabhasaḥ sūryaśatrur mahābalaḥ suptaghno yajñakopaś ca mahāpārśvo mahodaraḥ
english: Then Nikumbha, Rabhasas, Sūryaśatru the mighty, Suptaghna, Yajñakopa, Mahāpārśva, and Mahodara —

sanskrit: agniketuś ca durdharṣo raśmiketuś ca rākṣasaḥ indrajic ca mahātejā balavān rāvaṇātmajaḥ
english: Agniketu the fierce, Raśmiketu the rākṣasa, and Indrajit of great splendour, the powerful son of Rāvaṇa —

sanskrit: prahasto 'tha virūpākṣo vajradaṃṣṭro mahābalaḥ dhūmrākṣaś cātikāyaś ca durmukhaś caiva rākṣasaḥ
english: Prahasta, Virūpākṣa, Vajradaṃṣṭra the mighty, Dhūmrākṣa, Atikāya, and Durmukha the rākṣasa —

sanskrit: parighān paṭṭasān prāsāñ śaktiśūlaparaśvadhān cāpāni ca sabāṇāni khaḍgāṃś ca vipulāñ śitān
english: seizing iron clubs, broadswords, lances, spears, tridents, battle-axes, bows with arrows, and large sharp swords,

sanskrit: pragṛhya paramakruddhāḥ samutpatya ca rākṣasāḥ abruvan rāvaṇaṃ sarve pradīptā iva tejasā
english: those rākṣasas, in supreme fury, leaping up and blazing as if with energy, all spoke to Rāvaṇa:

sanskrit: adya rāmaṃ vadhiṣyāmaḥ sugrīvaṃ ca salakṣmaṇam kṛpaṇaṃ ca hanūmantaṃ laṅkā yena pradharṣitā
english: "Today we shall slay Rāma, Sugrīva with Lakṣmaṇa, and the wretched Hanūmat by whom Laṅkā was violated."

sanskrit: tān gṛhītāyudhān sarvān vārayitvā vibhīṣaṇaḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ punaḥ pratyupaveśya tān
english: Having restrained all of them who had taken up weapons, Vibhīṣaṇa made them sit down again and spoke with folded hands:

sanskrit: apy upāyais tribhis tāta yo 'rthaḥ prāptuṃ na śakyate tasya vikramakālāṃs tān yuktān āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "Dear one, the goal which cannot be attained by the three means — conciliation, gifts, and sowing division — has its proper times for the use of force, as the wise declare.

sanskrit: pramatteṣv abhiyukteṣu daivena prahateṣu ca vikramās tāta sidhyanti parīkṣya vidhinā kṛtāḥ
english: Feats of force succeed, dear one, when performed after due deliberation and in accordance with proper method, against those who are careless, beset by enemies, or struck down by fate.

sanskrit: apramattaṃ kathaṃ taṃ tu vijigīṣuṃ bale sthitam jitaroṣaṃ durādharṣaṃ pradharṣayitum icchatha
english: But how do you wish to assault him who is vigilant, who desires victory, who stands firm in strength, who has conquered his wrath, and who is hard to assail?

sanskrit: samudraṃ laṅghayitvā tu ghoraṃ nadanadīpatim kṛtaṃ hanumatā karma duṣkaraṃ tarkayeta kaḥ
english: Having crossed the terrible ocean, lord of rivers and streams — who could have imagined the feat accomplished by Hanūmat?

sanskrit: balāny aparimeyāni vīryāṇi ca niśācarāḥ pareṣāṃ sahasāvajñā na kartavyā kathaṃ cana
english: The strength and valour of enemies are immeasurable, O rangers of the night; sudden contempt for them must not be shown under any circumstances.

sanskrit: kiṃ ca rākṣasarājasya rāmeṇāpakṛtaṃ purā ājahāra janasthānād yasya bhāryāṃ yaśasvinaḥ
english: And moreover, what wrong was previously done to Rāma, the glorious one, by the king of rākṣasas — whose wife was carried away from Janasthāna?

sanskrit: kharo yady ativṛttas tu rāmeṇa nihato raṇe avaśyaṃ prāṇināṃ prāṇā rakṣitavyā yathā balam
english: If Khara overstepped and was slain by Rāma in battle, the lives of living beings must surely be protected to the best of one's ability.

sanskrit: etannimittaṃ vaidehī bhayaṃ naḥ sumahad bhavet āhṛtā sā parityājyā kalahārthe kṛte na kim
english: On account of this, the greatest fear would befall us; the abducted Vaidehī should be surrendered — why perpetuate a quarrel that has been provoked?

sanskrit: na naḥ kṣamaṃ vīryavatā tena dharmānuvartinā vairaṃ nirarthakaṃ kartuṃ dīyatām asya maithilī
english: It is not fitting for us to wage a pointless war against that valiant one who follows righteousness; let Maithilī be given to him.

sanskrit: yāvan na sagajāṃ sāśvāṃ bahuratnasamākulām purīṃ dārayate bāṇair dīyatām asya maithilī
english: Before he shatters the city — with its elephants, horses, and abundant treasures — with his arrows, let Maithilī be given to him.

sanskrit: yāvat sughorā mahatī durdharṣā harivāhinī nāvaskandati no laṅkāṃ tāvat sītā pradīyatām
english: Before his terrible, great, and invincible army of vānaras descends upon our Laṅkā, let Sītā be given back.

sanskrit: vinaśyed dhi purī laṅkā śūrāḥ sarve ca rākṣasāḥ rāmasya dayitā patnī na svayaṃ yadi dīyate
english: For the city of Laṅkā and all the heroic rākṣasas will surely perish if the beloved wife of Rāma is not willingly given back.

sanskrit: prasādaye tvāṃ bandhutvāt kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama hitaṃ pathyaṃ tv ahaṃ brūmi dīyatām asya maithilī
english: I implore you out of kinship — act upon my words; I speak what is beneficial and wholesome: let Maithilī be given to him.

sanskrit: purā śaratsūryamarīcisaṃnibhān navāgrapuṅkhān sudṛḍhān nṛpātmajaḥ sṛjaty amoghān viśikhān vadhāya te pradīyatāṃ dāśarathāya maithilī
english: Before the prince releases upon you his unfailing arrows — bright as the rays of the autumn sun, freshly fletched, well-strung — for your destruction, let Maithilī be given to the son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: tyajasva kopaṃ sukhadharmanāśanaṃ bhajasva dharmaṃ ratikīrtivardhanam prasīda jīvema saputrabāndhavāḥ pradīyatāṃ dāśarathāya maithilī
english: Abandon wrath, which destroys happiness and righteousness; embrace righteousness, which increases joy and fame; be gracious — let us live with our sons and kinsmen; let Maithilī be given to the son of Daśaratha.
